_about: Hand labels for every POISON-* finding in the published top-100 npm scan (docs/research/2026-10-top100-npm/summary.json). scripts/bench_poisoning.py precision refuses to run unless these labels cover every finding exactly once. Method: docs/poisoning.md#how-the-top-100-findings-were-labelled.
scanner_version: mcp-audit 0.21.0 (src/mcp_audit/analyzers/poisoning.py and mcp_client.build_runtime_server_config are unchanged from v0.21.0 to main at f9ba1ff)

label_definitions.true_positive: The text the finding points at is an attempt to make the agent do something the user did not ask for, or to hide content from the user.
label_definitions.false_positive: The text is ordinary documentation of the tool or its parameters.

basis_definitions.committed_evidence: The label follows from the evidence string committed in summary.json alone.
basis_definitions.review: The label comes from the review done with the 2026-10-22 scan, which had the full live tool definitions (about 6 MB, not committed; scripts/enumerate.py in the top-100 directory regenerates them). Its README: 'None of the poisoning findings in this corpus was a real attack.' On 2026-10-25 the published npm source of 51 of the 57 servers connect-summary.json lists as connected was read (never run; the other six are over 60 MB) for each matched phrase; every occurrence found was ordinary documentation of a parameter, a workflow step or the code itself.

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: The only characters POISON-060 matched across the corpus are U+FF08, U+FF0C, U+FF1A and U+FF1B: full-width parenthesis, comma, colon and semicolon, the normal punctuation of Chinese text. They are not letters, so they cannot disguise an English word; after normalization they become ( , : ; and no literal pattern fires on them.

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: A description of 2,000 characters or more. Length is the whole signal; the long descriptions are API reference text (the longest is a 40,325-character test-management tool), and the review found no instructions in them.

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: Workflow documentation of the shape "first call X to resolve the ID" between a server's own tools.

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: Next-step documentation, e.g. "After calling this tool, use <other tool> to run it".

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: A pointer to the right tool for a different task.

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: Parameter documentation of the shape "Override default <setting>" (for example a hostname or a result limit).

labels.label: false_positive
labels.why: Data-format documentation ("Base64 encoded file content or file path"); the nearby word that satisfied the co-occurrence gate is part of the same format description.
